| [QUESTION-216](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-216.md) | Does the output Fisher–Rao geometry agreement across language models replicate with released code, and does it fall when models are fitted to different laws while their activation geometry stays as it was, with only a small part of the shared eigenvector structure exceeding a fair law-matched null? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md). | [QUESTION-286](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-286.md) | Under smooth invertible changes of the parameter coordinates, which first-order frustration diagnoses among a learner's demands are invariant: pairwise Euclidean gradient angles, common strict first-order descent, or budgeted feasibility with the update geometry transported? | The coordinate part of [QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) (Active) settles it in full. Common strict descent, 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, is invariant under smooth invertible reparameterization. The sign of a Euclidean gradient inner product is not, and a negative inner product does not exclude common descent. A budgeted test is invariant when the metric is pulled back. These are the first three rows of A35 §2's table. | Answered |
